**Trader consensus on a 22°C high in Paris on August 29, 2026, reflects persistent cloud cover, light rain, and moderate southwesterly winds that have suppressed daytime heating.** Official forecasts and real-time observations from Météo-France-aligned sources and GFS model outputs indicate afternoon maxima stabilizing near 21–23°C (roughly 70–74°F), well below the late-August climatological average high of ~24°C. High humidity (70–80%) and limited solar insolation under overcast skies have kept the urban heat island effect muted, with peak readings around 22°C confirmed through the afternoon. The market-implied 94.7% probability for exactly 22°C aligns with this evidence-based range from authoritative meteorological data. 

Realistic challenges include unexpected sky clearing that boosts insolation or minor measurement variations at official stations, though current conditions and model consensus make significant deviation unlikely before resolution.

**Official National Weather Service forecasts for Denver on August 29, 2026, project a daily maximum near 93°F under mostly sunny skies shifting to a 30% chance of afternoon thunderstorms.** This places the expected high squarely in the 92–93°F bin, with nearby model runs and private forecasts showing a tight cluster between the low 90s and mid-90s depending on storm timing and cloud cover. Afternoon convection, driven by monsoon moisture and daytime heating, introduces the main uncertainty: early or widespread storms could enhance mixing and cap temperatures closer to 90–91°F, while delayed or localized activity would allow fuller solar heating toward 93°F or slightly above.

**Supporting context includes Denver’s late-August climatology (average high ~85°F) and observed morning readings in the low-to-mid 70s, with light southwest winds favoring gradual warming.** Model spreads reflect differences in boundary-layer moisture and convective initiation timing rather than large-scale pattern shifts, keeping the two leading bins nearly even in trader-implied odds. Resolution hinges on the official high reported from Denver International Airport or equivalent NWS observations by the end of the day.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Paris-Le Bourget Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 30 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=lfpb

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official forecasts from the Hong Kong Observatory position 29–30 °C as the most probable range for the daily maximum on August 30.** Multiple HKO updates issued on August 29 forecast a temperature range of 27–30 °C (or 27–31 °C in some bulletins) under mainly cloudy skies with scattered showers and thunderstorms. These conditions limit solar heating and align with the market’s leading implied probabilities of 47.5 % for 29 °C and 36.0 % for 30 °C.

A broad low-pressure trough over the northern South China Sea is sustaining unsettled weather, delivering frequent cloud cover, showers, and localized thunderstorms that suppress daytime peaks. Light southwest winds and high humidity (75–95 %) further moderate temperatures by enhancing evaporative cooling and reducing insolation. The pattern follows a slightly hotter August 29 (around 33 °C with brief sunny intervals) and contrasts with the August climatological mean daily maximum of 31.1 °C.

Model consensus and recent observational trends reinforce this outlook, with showers expected to be more widespread on August 30 than on preceding days. Resolution hinges on the official HKO recorded maximum at the King’s Park or Observatory site; any break in cloud cover could push readings toward 31 °C, while persistent rain would favor the lower end of the distribution.

Market-implied odds favoring 35°C or 36°C reflect trader weighting of these convective timing uncertainties against historical late-August maxima near 33–34°C, with new model runs and official updates likely to drive the narrow spread.

eventMetadata.context_description: Chongqing’s late-August heat is shaped by persistent subtropical high pressure, weak monsoon flow, and the city’s river valley topography that traps heat and moisture. Official forecasts from the China Meteorological Administration and ensemble models show a narrow range of possible daily maxima centered on 30–32 °C for 30 August, with small differences arising from cloud-cover timing, boundary-layer mixing, and the strength of downslope warming along the Yangtze. Historical climatology places the 1991–2020 average high near 31 °C, while urban heat-island effects can add 1–2 °C locally. The market’s tight clustering around 31 °C (34 %) and 30 °C (27.5 %) reflects this modest forecast spread and the resolution criteria tied to a single official station reading.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent heavy rainfall and thick cloud cover from the enhanced southwest monsoon (habagat) are the main factors capping Manila's daytime highs for August 30, favoring market-implied probabilities clustered around 29–31°C. Official PAGASA guidance and multiple forecast models indicate monsoon rains with 80–100% precipitation chances, strong southwesterly winds, and widespread overcast skies that limit insolation and suppress temperatures below the typical 31°C August average. A developing strong El Niño adds longer-term context for altered rainfall patterns but reinforces near-term habagat enhancement over western Luzon. Recent flooding and red rainfall warnings on August 29 confirm these conditions are already established, with limited model spread pointing to modest warming only if breaks in clouds occur. Traders appear to weigh the high likelihood of continued suppression against modest upside if monsoon intensity eases slightly overnight.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent rainfall and clearing skies are the main drivers positioning 34–35°C as the leading outcomes for Chongqing’s highest temperature on August 31.** 

A strong rain event from August 28–30 brought heavy downpours, localized storms, and gusty winds across western and central Chongqing, sharply lowering daytime highs to the 27–33°C range in many districts and interrupting the prior heatwave that saw peaks above 37°C (with one site reaching 40.7°C). By August 30 night into the 31st, official Chongqing Meteorological Bureau guidance and multiple forecast models (including Yr.no and Worldmeteo) show skies turning mostly cloudy to sunny with only isolated showers possible, allowing renewed solar heating. 

Forecast highs for the 31st cluster tightly around 34°C (center-city guidance often cites 25–34°C), with some ensemble members and international models (e.g., WeatherBug) reaching 35°C under clearer conditions. Historical late-August baselines for Chongqing hover near 31°C, so the post-rain recovery supports a modest rebound but not an immediate return to earlier extremes. 

Market-implied odds reflect this consensus: 35°C leads at 45% and 34°C at 25%, while higher values (36°C+) remain lower-probability outliers pending final model runs and any last-minute cloud or moisture changes. The next official updates from the Chongqing Meteorological Bureau and global ensembles will be the key near-term catalysts.
